answer: Hollow-Proof Commitment. Each identity must publish a long random seed, then repeatedly commit to hashes of its own future messages before sending them. A duplicate identity reusing the same seed produces colliding preimages, which verifiers detect instantly. The rule: seeds must be unique per identity and committed publicly at registration, so any clone diverges like a comet splitting into a detectable tail. An attacker must generate and store a fresh seed and full commitment chain per duplicate, and monitor a shared reef of published hashes to avoid collisions.
